sun.upright:
An argument you can win in two minutes is hard for an Aries Sun to walk past, and you like being known as someone who doesn't back off. The Five of Swords hands you that kind of win and then leaves you standing in the field holding the swords, with the other two already halfway down the hill. Venus is the planet behind this card, and Venus is in detriment in Aries, the sign opposite her own Libra. So the part of you that cares about keeping people close has to work against your grain, and when you're fired up it mostly doesn't get a vote.

Air feeds fire, and Aquarius sits a sextile from Aries, so the card's cool cleverness catches in you fast. You'll have the sharp line, the logical case, the point nobody can answer. To you it feels like honesty, even a kind of courage, because you only said what everyone else was thinking. What you don't always clock is the look on the other person's face, the one that means they've stopped arguing because they've given up on you. Aries Suns I've read for tend to get the win in about two minutes and the bill a month later, when they're quietly left off an invitation.

At work it's the meeting where you took apart a colleague's proposal in front of the boss, correctly, and now they route things around you. With a sibling it's the old argument you've won eleven times and they still bring up every Christmas. In a relationship it's being right about the dishes, again. Before the next argument you're sure you'll win, decide what you'd actually like to have at the end of it, and say that first.
sun.reversed:
For everyone else the fight is finished. For an Aries Sun with this card upside down it's still going, re-run in your head with better lines each time. Mars's sign doesn't do lingering well, and Venus in detriment here has no easy route to the apology or the handshake, so the conflict just sits. Or you lost, which Aries takes harder than it lets on, and the loss has quietly turned into a reason to prove something to a person who moved on weeks ago.

At work that looks like a rivalry only one of you is still in. With a friend it's the message you've drafted three times that opens with sorry and ends with a dig. Pride is what's holding it up. Send the version with the apology and cut the last line. If you can't manage that, stop drafting for a fortnight and see how much of it still matters.

moon.upright:
Quick to flare and quick to forget, an Aries Moon needs to let a feeling out the moment it arrives. Anger is fast with you and it's usually gone by lunch. The Five of Swords on your tides means there's been a scrap, or one's brewing, and part of you is enjoying it more than you'd admit. The trouble is the Aquarius half of the card. Air feeds fire, the two signs are a sextile apart, and the card's cool, precise way of being right lends your temper an edge it doesn't normally have. You don't just get cross. You get cross with footnotes.

Venus is in detriment in Aries, so warmth has a hard time getting through while you're heated. She isn't a total stranger to your sign, though. She rules its last ten degrees, the decan of the Four of Wands, the card of friends gathered at the gate to welcome someone home. That's the other half of what an Aries Moon needs, and it gets lost in the heat. Once the flare has passed you want to be let straight back in, no post-mortem. The people you argued with often need a day longer than you, and that lag can feel like being punished.

With a partner this is the eleven o'clock fight you've forgotten by breakfast and they haven't. With housemates it's the note on the fridge written while you were still hot. Your body carries it as a jaw that aches in the morning. Say the angry thing if you have to. Then go back within the hour and say the second thing, the one about wanting to be friends again.
moon.reversed:
An Aries Moon's temper usually clears in minutes. With the card reversed it gets stuck. Venus in detriment has nowhere to put the hurt, so it simmers, and you catch yourself picking small fights that aren't about anything, the tone of a text, a door shut too loudly. Or it runs the other way and you swallow the anger to keep the peace, which you're terrible at, and it leaks out as sarcasm.

Home gets it first, whoever's closest, and your sleep goes light and hot. At work it's the snappy reply to an email that didn't deserve it. Get the heat out of your body before you deal with the person. Run, dig, carry something heavy up the stairs. Then find the one thing that actually upset you and say that, in about a sentence, to the person it concerns.

rising.upright:
Within five minutes of meeting Aries rising, people often feel they've been tested, and with this card drawn for your mask they probably have. You come in quick and a bit competitive, and the card adds a cool debating edge. Aquarius and Aries are sextile, air feeding fire, so your wit catches fast and people can see it catching. In a new room you're often the one who says the clever, slightly cutting thing that gets the laugh.

The cost is that Venus sits in detriment in your rising sign. Charm is her whole job, and at the Aries doorway she's pushing uphill, so the warmth that would soften your edge tends to arrive late, after the first impression has already set. You'd call it banter. You spar because you like people. Strangers don't always know that, and a fair few take the joke personally and never mention it. You won't find out which ones. They'll just be a shade cooler with you from then on.

At a new job it's the sharp comment in the first team meeting that earns you a reputation, only some of it flattering. On a first date it's teasing that lands wrong with someone who hasn't learned your style yet. With a new neighbour it's winning the parking argument in your first week in the street. Let your first joke with someone new be at your own expense, and watch what that does to the rest of the conversation.
rising.reversed:
Walking in braced for a fight that isn't there is the reversed version of this card for Aries rising. The competitive edge fires early, before anyone's pushed, and new people meet the armour instead of you. The other version is the Aries Ascendant who's been burned, who lost an argument in public and now comes into rooms carefully, holding back the quick remark and feeling oddly muted.

New colleagues react to both. In the first case they're wary of you. In the second they decide you're quieter than you are and hand the good projects to someone louder. A first meeting with someone new is a good place to find out which version is running. Walk in having decided there's nothing to win, and ask them about their day before you say anything clever.

sun.upright:
Venus rules Taurus, so when a Taurus Sun draws the Five of Swords it's your own planet turning up, dressed in a way you might not recognise. This is Venus in Aquarius. The same planet that loves good food, a warm room and people you can rely on has gone somewhere cold and principled, where being right comes first. Aquarius squares Taurus, two fixed signs at right angles, and you'll feel that as a standoff where neither side is going to move first.

Fixed earth wants proof. Fixed air wants the principle. So the fight this card usually points to for you is about how things should be done, where you've got the evidence and the other person has an argument, and nobody budges. It feels, while you're in it, like being reasonable. You're only asking for what's fair, and you've been patient for ages. The trouble is that a Taurus Sun can hold a position for a very long time, and the card is asking whether this particular one is worth what it's costing to hold, the friendship or the goodwill or just the ease you normally live in.

With money this is the dispute with a landlord or a tradesperson over a few hundred dollars that has eaten three months of your evenings. At work it's the process you built that someone new wants to change, and your refusal, which is correct and is also wearing you out. With family it's the house, or the will, or the thing everyone's being polite about. Work out what this fight has cost you so far, in money or in hours. Write the figure down and look at it before your next move.
sun.reversed:
A Taurus Sun with this card reversed tends to keep a grudge the way it keeps anything valuable, safely and for years. Venus is at home in your sign, and upside down she gets possessive about the hurt itself. You won't fight about it. You just won't forgive it, and the person who did it can feel the temperature drop whenever they're in a room with you.

Two years on, the colleague from that meeting still gets perfect civility from you and no trust at all. In the family it's the relative you haven't forgiven for something at a wedding. With money it's refusing to deal with someone even when they're the best person for the job. Ask yourself honestly what keeping this one gives you. If the answer is mostly the feeling of being in the right, see whether you'd swap that for one easy afternoon in their company.

moon.upright:
Rows get into a Taurus Moon's body in a way they don't with most signs. You need things steady, good sleep, a meal at the usual time, people who are the same from one week to the next, and the Five of Swords turns up in your tides when that steadiness has been knocked. Venus is your Moon's ruler, so the planet of this card has real say over how you feel. Here she's in Aquarius, which squares Taurus, and Aquarian Venus handles hurt by getting cool and logical about it. That's just not how you're made.

Air and earth don't mix well. One is talk and the other is proof. When someone argues with you, however cleverly, some part of you won't believe a word until it's been shown in how they behave. So you go quiet and dig in. The other person reads that as sulking, or as losing, and may walk off thinking they've won. You're nowhere near finished. Fixed earth takes weeks to settle after a disturbance, and your body keeps the account, a stiff neck, comfort eating, a tiredness you can't sleep off.

With a partner this looks like the argument that got settled in words on Sunday and that you're still carrying on Thursday. At home it's needing the house back to normal before you can feel normal, and resenting anyone who won't let it be. With a friend it's the slow withdrawal after they said something sharp in company. Do something physical and slow first, a bath, a long walk, cooking for yourself. Then decide whether the argument still needs finishing.
moon.reversed:
Keeping the peace at any price is how this card often shows up reversed on a Taurus Moon. You'd sooner eat the hurt than have the argument, so you do, and it sits in your stomach, sometimes literally. Venus rules your Moon, and when her Aquarian side is blocked she goes for comfort instead of conversation, the extra glass, the online order, another night on the couch that fixes nothing.

Your partner hears 'it's fine' in a tone everyone in the house knows is a lie. At work you let someone take a bit more of your time, your desk, your credit, because objecting feels like it would cause a bigger upset. Pick one small thing you've let slide and object to it, calmly, in a single sentence. Then carry on with your evening as normal and notice that nothing collapsed.

rising.upright:
With Taurus rising, Venus is your chart ruler, since she rules the sign on your Ascendant. So the Five of Swords, which is Venus in Aquarius, lands right on the planet that shapes how people meet you. Normally that's pleasant and unhurried, somebody easy to be around and hard to push. This card puts a firmer edge on the easy manner. The square between Aquarius and Taurus is two fixed signs at odds, and at first contact it can make you look as if you've already made up your mind.

Often you have. Taurus rising doesn't move quickly and doesn't move for talk, and with air and earth pulling against each other here, a clever argument from a stranger can make you less likely to agree with them. It seems like plain good sense to you. You'll wait and see what they actually do. What they see is a pleasant face that won't give an inch, and some of them take that as a challenge. That's where this card's contests come from for you. Somebody new decides to win you round, and you decide they won't.

At a new job it's the manager who pushes a change in week one and meets a very polite wall. In a negotiation it's you getting the better deal simply by not blinking, and the other side leaving sour. On a date it's being so calm about what you want that the other person feels overruled on where to eat. When somebody new pushes, try giving them one small thing they've asked for straight away. You can hold firm on the rest.
rising.reversed:
Stillness can look like a verdict on a Taurus Ascendant, and with the card reversed people are reading it that way. You go quiet and pleasant when a conversation turns sharp, and they take the quiet as disapproval. Or it flips, and you give way far too easily to someone pushy because the friction is so unpleasant, and then resent the outcome for months.

In meetings it's being talked out of an idea you'd have won if you'd held your ground. Socially it's the acquaintance who treats your easygoing manner as permission and keeps pushing. With a builder, a seller or a landlord, it's agreeing to a price on the spot to end the awkwardness. Give yourself a stock phrase for these moments, something like 'let me think about it and get back to you', and use it before agreeing to anything.

sun.upright:
Air card, air sign. The Five of Swords belongs to Aquarius, which is trine to Gemini, so for a Gemini Sun this card speaks your language with no accent at all. That's the gift and the problem. Venus has no special standing in Gemini and takes her cues from your ruler, Mercury, so affection in you comes out as wit. You show you like someone by sparring with them. You're proud of being quick, and a lot of how you want to be seen rests on having the better line.

Same element means amplification, for better and for too much. The debate you started for fun turns real somewhere around the third exchange, and you miss the moment it tipped, because for you it was still a game. The other person didn't miss it. Gemini Suns can argue either side of anything, and sometimes you're defending a view you don't even hold, just because it's the more interesting one, and the person across from you thinks you mean it. Winning that sort of argument is fun for about ten minutes. Then there's a small hollow feeling and you tell yourself it's boredom.

In a group chat it's the joke that landed on someone who's been quiet ever since. At work it's the colleague you out-talked in a meeting who now takes their ideas to someone else. With a brother or sister it's the old habit of scoring points at the dinner table. Once in a while, when you've made a sharp point, stop there. Let the other person have the next word and actually take in what they say.
sun.reversed:
Talking your way round a conflict is the reversed Five of Swords for a Gemini Sun. You're very good at changing the subject, making a joke, reframing the whole thing so nobody quite lost. Air on air, Venus coloured by Mercury, and the words start doing all the work of avoiding. The row never happens, and neither does the repair.

Your partner has watched you dodge the same argument so many times it's become a running joke, and they've stopped finding it funny. At work it's the difficult email answered with a long, friendly message that says nothing. With a friend it's pretending you didn't notice the dig. Say one plain sentence about the actual problem, with no joke on the end of it. Then stop talking for a bit and let it sit.

moon.upright:
Who said what, what they really meant, what you should have said back. That's the loop a Gemini Moon gets into when the Five of Swords shows up in its tides. You process feelings by talking them through, preferably with several people and in several versions, and there's been a conflict somewhere near you that you haven't finished processing. Venus is only a guest in Gemini and takes her colour from Mercury, so even your hurt comes out as commentary.

Aquarius and Gemini share the air element and sit in trine, so the card and your Moon feed each other without effort. That can be useful. You'll see the whole situation clearly, both sides, the history, the patterns. It can also mean the feeling never gets felt, only described, and the more cleverly you describe it the further off it seems. You'll have told three friends and assumed that dealt with it. Then you wake at two in the morning with your mind still running the argument and no idea why it hasn't gone.

With friends it can look like gathering support for your side a little too efficiently. With a partner it's the post-mortem on a row that goes on so long it turns into a second row. Your sleep shows it first, and your hands, never far from the phone. Once you've told the story twice, stop telling it. Go for a walk without your phone and notice what's left when there's nobody to tell.
moon.reversed:
The argument finished days ago, but a Gemini Moon with this card reversed is still rehearsing it, trying out better answers in the shower and on the bus. Air amplifying air turns the whole thing into noise. Or you've decided to feel nothing about it at all, and you're keeping so busy with chat and plans that there's never a quiet minute for it to land.

Sleep goes restless and full of talking. With friends you're oddly flippant about something that clearly hurt. Your partner gets the sudden bright change of subject whenever it comes near. Write the argument out once, all of it, including the bits where you weren't at your best. Then close the notebook and do something with your hands for an hour.

rising.upright:
Sparring is how Gemini rising says hello, and this card gives the sparring a real edge. Venus is a visitor in Gemini, borrowing Mercury's speed, and with Aquarius trine your rising sign the card's cool cleverness comes very naturally to you. Strangers find you funny and hard to get the better of. You'll often win the first exchange at a party without quite meaning to.

Same element means the card amplifies what's already there. On a good day that's charm. On a less good one it's a habit of testing new people with a bit of teasing, seeing if they can keep up, and losing interest in the ones who can't. It's play, mostly, and you'd say so if asked. What you miss is the person who took it as a put-down and has quietly decided you're a bit unkind. Have a look at the two figures walking off in the background of the card. In real life there's usually one of them, and they rarely tell you why they left.

At a job interview it's the smart answer that makes the panel laugh and makes one of them feel slightly foolish. With new neighbours it's the witty remark about their renovation. On a date it's being so entertaining that the other person never gets a word in and goes home feeling outshone. With the next new person you meet, let them be the funny one for a while. Laugh at their jokes properly.
rising.reversed:
You might be meeting new people with a joke already loaded, ready to get in first before anyone can make you look silly. That's the defensive turn this card takes reversed on a Gemini Ascendant. Or you've been on the wrong end of someone else's cleverness lately and gone unusually quiet in company, checking every remark before you make it.

New colleagues can't tell whether you're joking or having a go. Socially you might leave a gathering early because the banter felt like a contest you didn't have the energy for. Online it's the comment you fired at a stranger and then thought about all evening. In your next few first meetings, say something sincere before you say something clever, even if it's only that you're glad to be there.

sun.upright:
Cancer Suns fight hardest for other people. You'll let a slight to yourself go for years, and then somebody says one thing about your kid or your mum and you're across the room. The Five of Swords for a Cancer Sun is very often that kind of conflict, taken on in someone's defence, and won, and followed by a strange empty feeling on the drive home. Aquarius and Cancer are quincunx, five signs apart with nothing in common. Cool principle and warm loyalty don't share a language, so every argument between them needs constant small translations.

Venus is only a visitor in your sign and takes her colour from the Moon, your ruler, so the card's cold, clever edge comes to you soaked in feeling. That makes it hurt more, and it makes it messier. You don't enjoy winning. You win because you felt you had to, and afterwards you're counting the damage. Venus does have a real place in Cancer, though. She rules its first ten degrees, the decan of the Two of Cups, the card of two people making a pledge to each other. That's what you actually want out of any fight, the bond made safe, and this card wins the point and leaves the bond a bit bruised.

At home this is the family row where you took a side and now half the family is careful around you. At work it's the team you protected from a bad decision, at some cost to how the boss sees you. With a friend it's the argument you had on their behalf that they never asked you to have. Next time, ask the person you're defending whether they want you to step in at all. Then do what they say.
sun.reversed:
Inside the shell is where the conflict goes when this card reverses for a Cancer Sun. You don't have the argument. You go quiet, keep the hurt, and remember it in detail, and the other person may not know there's been a falling-out at all. The Moon rules your sign and Venus borrows her moods here, so a grievance nobody's said aloud can colour weeks of your life.

Families are where it lives longest, the relative you're polite to at every gathering and haven't forgiven since that thing years ago. At work it's being hurt that your part wasn't mentioned, saying nothing, and withdrawing a little effort without ever deciding to. Choose the one person you're quietly holding something against. Tell them the grievance once, plainly, without the history attached, and see what they do with it.

moon.upright:
The two figures walking away in the background of the Five of Swords, one with his face in his hands, are often where a Cancer Moon finds itself with this card. You feel conflict deeply and you take it home with you, and with the Moon ruling your sign, your moods follow whoever's closest. When someone you love goes cool and clever on you, which is exactly what Venus in Aquarius does in an argument, it can feel like being locked out of your own house.

Air and water are neutral to each other. They neither clash nor get on, and they have to be introduced. Aquarius and Cancer are quincunx as well, so the logic of the argument and the feeling of it keep missing each other. The other person has made a reasonable case. You can see it's reasonable, and it doesn't touch the hurt at all, and being told you're being illogical makes it worse. What really stings is that someone you trusted was willing to win against you. Losing the actual point barely comes into it.

With a partner it's the calm, rational discussion that left you in tears in the bathroom afterwards. With a parent it's the old pattern where their being right always counted for more than you being heard. Your stomach and your sleep carry it. Venus rules the first decan of your sign, the Two of Cups, and that card is about two people on the same side. Ask for that, in so many words. Tell the person you need them on your side for five minutes before anyone works out who was right.
moon.reversed:
'I'm over it,' you've said, and a Cancer Moon with this card reversed rarely is. The hurt from the conflict has gone underground and it's running things from there. The Moon's sign keeps an excellent record. So you're a shade less warm with that person, you remember to mention something they got wrong, you're tired in a way sleep doesn't touch.

It can turn on you as well, going over something you said in a fight and feeling sick about it for days. Family meals carry it, the atmosphere telling everyone what nobody's saying. Make one small gesture of care towards the person, a cup of tea, a message about something else entirely, without mentioning the argument. Watch whether it softens anything, in them or in you.

rising.upright:
Tension in a room reaches Cancer rising before anyone speaks, and when this is the card on your Ascendant, the rooms you walk into tend to be tense ones. Somebody's just had words, a team has split into camps, the family's got a feud on. People read you as gentle and a little guarded, and they'll often try to recruit you, because you look like someone who'll take their side.

The card and your rising sign are quincunx, with nothing natural between them and everything needing adjustment. Venus is only a guest in Cancer, borrowing the Moon's sensitivity, so the card's clever, detached way of handling conflict doesn't sit well on you. You try the cool approach and it comes out prickly. Or you try to stay out of it and get pulled in anyway, because you can't bear the feeling in the room. To people watching, you can look like the one causing the tension, simply because you're the one visibly reacting to it.

At a new job you land in the middle of an old dispute and both sides assume you're with them. In a friendship group you become the one everyone vents to, which slowly makes you part of the fight. With in-laws it's being careful at every visit because you once said the wrong thing. When you feel yourself being drawn into someone else's conflict, say out loud that you'd prefer to stay out of it. Most people take that far better than you expect.
rising.reversed:
The shell goes up hard on a Cancer Ascendant when this card is reversed. You meet new people already expecting to be hurt, and the defensiveness can come across as coldness or even hostility, which is the opposite of what you feel. Sometimes it's the sideways approach overdone, the pointed remark in place of the direct request, and people can't work out why you seem cross with them.

Your first few weeks somewhere new can get you labelled difficult or aloof. With a new partner's family it's a small comment that turns into a cool distance on your side. Online it's taking something personally from someone who didn't mean it that way. Before you decide someone's against you, ask them one straightforward question about what they meant. Your read on hostility at first contact is often wrong, and it's worth checking.

sun.upright:
Leo and Aquarius sit across the zodiac from each other, and the Five of Swords belongs to the Aquarius end of that line. So for a Leo Sun this card is the opposite point of view turning up in your own life, the cool, group-minded, prove-it-with-logic side of the axis you were born facing. Leo wants to be seen doing something that matters, generously and with a bit of style. This card is about a win that sends people home early, which is about the last thing a Leo Sun is after.

Venus has no particular standing in Leo. She's a guest there and takes her tone from the Sun, so your affection is warm, loud and a little bit about you. That's usually lovely. The Aquarian Venus in this card is colder and more interested in being right, and when the two meet in an argument, air feeds fire and things catch fast. You won't just make your point. You'll make it well, in front of people, and enjoy the room going quiet. Leo pride is a real thing, and I've seen plenty of Leo Suns win a fight they didn't care about simply because backing down in public felt impossible.

Think of the pitch you defended so hard that the person who questioned it has avoided you ever since. Or the dinner party where you corrected your partner and got the laugh. A younger colleague, or your own kid, might be on the receiving end too, when you were right about something they needed to work out for themselves. Next time someone challenges you with other people watching, thank them for the question and save your answer for later, in private.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, this card often catches a Leo Sun after the fight, sulking in some style. You lost the argument, or you won it and nobody clapped, and your pride has taken it harder than you let anyone see. With the Sun colouring Venus in your sign, a knock to how you're seen goes straight to how you feel about yourself, and the pull of the opposition keeps dragging you back to the other person's cold, correct version of events.

At work you might be withdrawing your enthusiasm from a project because someone else got the credit. Friends may have noticed the grand gestures have stopped, at least toward the people who didn't appreciate the last one. Your partner could be waiting weeks for an apology you're waiting for them to make. Make the first warm move yourself, something generous and a bit public, and don't attach a speech to it.

moon.upright:
What a Leo Moon needs in order to feel safe is fairly simple and slightly embarrassing to admit. You need to be adored by the people you love, and told so, often. So a card about a cold, clever argument sits badly in your tides. The card is Venus in Aquarius, the sign opposite yours, and the Aquarian way of handling a hurt is to go distant and reasonable. Yours is to want someone to come and put their arms round you. When the person you're fighting with goes cool, you take it as being loved less, and then you get louder.

Air feeds fire, so the chill from the other side doesn't settle you. It fans you. Venus is only a guest in Leo and follows the Sun's lead, so what you feel, you feel with your whole chest, and a row with someone close can flatten you for a day in a way people who know you as the bright one would never guess. Underneath the drama there's usually something quite young going on. You're checking whether you still matter to them.

Your partner might think the argument was about the washing-up. For you it turned, somewhere in the middle, into whether they even notice you. With a parent there can be an old habit of performing to get their attention, and feeling hollow when it works. You'll sleep badly and run hot. When it happens, skip the argument and ask for the thing directly, a hug, an evening together, a compliment you'd like to hear.
moon.reversed:
Hurt pride goes underground on a Leo Moon when the card is upside down. You'd never admit a quarrel got to you, so you act fine, a little too fine, cheerful and busy and slightly regal about it. The opposition from Aquarius gives you the tools for this, a cool front that isn't really yours. Inside, you're keeping a list of who didn't check on you.

Home and close friendships carry most of it. You stop offering warmth first and wait to see who notices, and the ones who don't get quietly demoted. Your energy dips in a way that looks like ordinary tiredness. Tell one person you trust that you were hurt, in those words, without making a joke of it. Leo Moons are usually surprised by how kindly that gets received.

rising.upright:
People notice Leo rising when it walks in, and with the Five of Swords drawn for your mask they're noticing someone who looks ready to win. There's a useful bit of chart geometry here. With Leo on your Ascendant, Aquarius sits on the cusp of your seventh house, the house of whoever's standing opposite you, so the cool, clever opponent in this card is exactly the kind of person your chart keeps putting across the table. Rivals, sharp colleagues, a partner who argues back.

The opposition between the two signs is a pull between showing yourself off and fitting in with the group, and since air feeds fire, the pull is quick and hot. When someone new challenges you, your instinct is to perform, to be funnier and surer of yourself than they are. It works. The room is usually on your side by the end. Venus in Leo is a visitor who takes her lead from the Sun, and her charm here is big and warm. That's what saves you in most of these exchanges, and also what makes it sting for the person you beat, because you did it so pleasantly.

Picture your first week in a new team, taking over a meeting, and the quieter colleague who decided on the spot that you were a show-off. Or the friend of a friend at a barbecue who kept trying to top your stories, and who you comfortably outdid. Dates go this way too, a small debate won so charmingly they don't notice they lost until they're home. In the next room where someone's clearly trying to compete with you, give them the floor for the first half hour and see what they're really like.
rising.reversed:
The performance gets defensive on a Leo Ascendant when this card flips. You walk into a new place already expecting to be challenged, so you come in bigger than you need to, and people who'd have liked you find you a bit much. Or a recent public loss has you holding back, which on Leo rising reads as sulky, since everyone's used to you being the warm one in the room.

A new team, a presentation, somebody senior watching how you take a question, these are the places it gets noticed. Socially you're either the loudest at the party or oddly absent from it. With Aquarius on the seventh-house cusp, it can also show as choosing the same cool, critical kind of partner and then fighting them. Next time you're introduced to someone, ask them a question before you tell them anything about yourself.

sun.upright:
Being useful and being right about the details is a lot of how a Virgo Sun wants to be known, and this card is about being right and ending up with nobody left to be useful to. Venus is in fall in Virgo. It's the sign where her gift for affection has the hardest time being heard, so she gets indirect. Care comes out as correction. You fix someone's spreadsheet, point out the mistake in the booking, suggest a better way to fold the towels, and you mean it kindly, and they hear criticism.

Aquarius and Virgo are quincunx, five signs apart with nothing in common, and air and earth pull against each other besides. The card thinks in principles and your Sun thinks in the actual job in front of it, so the fights this card points to are usually about method, the right way to do a thing. You'll very often be correct, which is what makes it so hard to let go. There's a softer thread, though. Venus rules the middle ten degrees of Virgo, the decan of the Nine of Pentacles, a woman alone in a garden she made herself, and that's the pride you're really after, quiet competence and something good that's yours.

Somewhere there's a colleague whose sloppy report you rewrote, and who hasn't spoken to you since. At home your partner may have stopped helping in the kitchen because you always redo it. You can be just as hard on yourself, treating a missed week at the gym as if it were a character flaw. Pick one thing someone else did badly and leave it exactly as they did it.
sun.reversed:
This card reversed can turn a Virgo Sun's sharpness on itself. The argument you're losing is the one in your own head, where you go back over what you said in a meeting and find eleven things wrong with it. Venus in fall can't get much kindness through to you either. Or the critic goes quiet in public and gets very busy in private, keeping a list of everyone's mistakes that you'll never send.

It looks like staying late to fix something that wasn't your job, and then resenting the people who went home. Friends get helpful advice they didn't ask for, and give you a slightly tight smile. Your stomach and your sleep tend to pay for all of it. Write down one thing you did well this week, and one thing someone else did well, and tell them.

moon.upright:
Order is how a Virgo Moon settles itself. Kitchen clean, list done, the week planned, and then you can breathe. The Five of Swords stirs up the kind of conflict that won't fit in a list. Someone has been clever and cold with you, or you've been that with them, and the whole thing is untidy in a way that gets under your skin. Your Moon's sign is where Venus is in fall, which means comfort and affection have a hard time getting to you directly. You look after people by doing things for them, and you'd like to be looked after the same way, though you rarely ask.

Air and earth are opposed elements, and the card's Aquarian air runs on theory. Your Moon runs on what's actually been done. So when someone argues their way out of a promise, however well they argue, it feels to you like a small betrayal, and you keep turning it over. The quincunx between the two signs means there's no natural bridge. You'll be adjusting all the time, trying to be reasonable about something that hurts. A lot of Virgo Moons I've seen get run down at the tail end of a conflict, catching whatever's going round, as if the body waited until it was safe to stop.

Your partner promised to do the job and didn't, and gave you a neat explanation instead. A manager talks about fairness while handing your task to someone else. You clean the bathroom at midnight after an argument. Let yourself be looked after once, properly, dinner cooked for you and the dishes done by someone else, and let it count.
moon.reversed:
A conflict you haven't been able to resolve gets turned into jobs when a Virgo Moon has this card reversed. The drawers get sorted, the inbox cleared, anything that feels like control. Venus in fall can't get the tenderness through, so you manage the feeling instead. Or you've gone the other way and agreed to everything to avoid friction, then quietly done all the extra work yourself.

Sleep goes first, then digestion, then patience. You over-prepare for a meeting with someone you had words with. You apologise to a friend for things that weren't your fault, just so it's over. Spend twenty minutes doing something with your hands that has no right way to do it, kneading dough or pulling weeds, and let the argument sit unsolved while you do.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising comes across as careful, capable and a bit hard to impress, and people tend to straighten up around you without knowing why. With this card over it, that careful manner has an edge. You spot the flaw in someone's plan within minutes, and it shows on your face before you've said a word. Venus is in fall in your rising sign, so warmth at first meeting isn't your strong suit. You show interest by paying close attention, which strangers can mistake for inspection.

The card's style and yours need constant adjusting, since Aquarius and Virgo are quincunx. Aquarius will argue a principle in the abstract. You'll point to the exact line where the principle breaks. Air and earth rub against each other here, talk against proof, and you're always on the proof side. That makes you very hard to beat in a first exchange, and it can leave the other person feeling caught out. Mercury rules your rising sign as well, which is why, when you feel pushed, you get more exact and a good deal cooler.

In a job interview this might be the correction you gave the interviewer about their own company, accurate and quite possibly unhelpful to you. A new friend tells a story in front of other people and you gently fact-check it. A new client sends a brief and you point out its problems before you've built any goodwill. Hold your first correction back with someone new. Write it down and bring it up the second time you meet, when they already know you're on their side.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, this card can make a Virgo Ascendant so worried about seeming critical that you say almost nothing on first meeting. People take the quiet for judgement anyway, which is the unfair part. Or the old edge comes out sharper than you meant, a small correction in the first five minutes that sets the tone for months, and Venus in fall does very little to soften it.

New workplaces and new friend groups are where it shows. You might hang back from a group you'd like to join because you suspect they've already sized you up. A polite note to a new neighbour about the bins reads as a complaint. Try a compliment at the start of your next few first meetings, a real and specific one. It's easier than it sounds, since you've noticed everything anyway.

sun.upright:
Venus rules Libra, so for a Libra Sun this card is your own planet showing you its colder side. You want to be known as fair, easy to be around and good with people, the one who can see both sides. The Five of Swords is Venus in Aquarius, and there she cares about being right on principle, about fairness as an idea, and she'll let a relationship take damage to defend it. It's the same planet. It just isn't the version you usually lead with.

Aquarius and Libra are trine, both air, so the card's cool reasoning comes to you without any friction at all. That's the risk. The same element turns up whatever's already there, the good and the too much. You can build a beautifully balanced argument for why you're right, weigh every side, concede the small points gracefully, and still leave the other person flattened, because you've been so reasonable they've got nowhere to stand. Libra Suns tend to think of themselves as the peacemaker, and it can be a real shock to realise you've just won a fight on points and made someone feel small.

The fair process you designed at work happens to favour your side. The calm, very sensible discussion about where to spend the holidays is one you somehow always win. And when two friends fall out, you've quietly decided who was in the wrong, and it's shaping who gets invited. Justice is Libra's own card, and she holds scales. Ask yourself honestly which side of this you'd come down on if it were somebody else's argument.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, the card can freeze a Libra Sun in the middle of a conflict it doesn't know how to leave. You won't pick a side, because you can see both, so you hover and smooth things over and let the problem run much longer than it needed to. Venus at home in your sign wants harmony badly, and blocked, she'll pay nearly any price for a quiet room.

In meetings you find yourself agreeing with whoever spoke last. Two friends who've fallen out both still confide in you, and you carry messages between them. You said yes to a holiday you didn't want, and it'll come out in a tense moment months later. Take one side, in one conflict, and say so plainly. Then see how the people involved treat you afterwards.

moon.upright:
Nobody sleeps well in a house where people aren't speaking, but a Libra Moon sleeps worst of all. You need the people around you to be on good terms, and you'll quietly do a great deal of work to keep them that way. Venus rules your Moon's sign, so the planet in this card goes straight to your feelings. Here she's in Aquarius, cool and principled, willing to have the argument and live with the chill afterwards. That's a way of being you understand in your head and can't stand in your stomach.

Libra and Aquarius are trine, both air, so the card's logic sits comfortably in you. You'll argue the thing out very well. The trouble is that your Moon doesn't feel safe after winning. It feels safe when everyone's friends again. So you may win the point and then spend the evening trying to make it up to the person you beat, or concede something you believed in just to get the warmth back. Libra Moons I've read for often can't sleep on an argument. They need it settled before bed, and not everyone they live with works that way.

There's the talk you insist on having at eleven at night. The group holiday where two people fell out and you spent the week mediating. The knot in your stomach whenever there's tension in the office. Try going to bed on an unfinished argument once, on purpose, and notice that it's still fixable in the morning.
moon.reversed:
Keeping everybody happy has a cost, and a Libra Moon under this reversed card has usually been paying it for a while. Venus is at home in your sign, and upside down she over-gives, agreeing, softening, swallowing the thing you actually wanted to say. The resentment doesn't vanish. It turns up as a cool politeness that the people close to you can feel and can't quite name.

You're lovely to everyone at home and privately exhausted. There's a favour you said yes to that you're dreading. Your partner asks what you think, and you've lost track, because you've been so busy finding the middle. Next time someone asks what you'd like, answer in the first five seconds, before you've checked their face.

rising.upright:
The Five of Swords falls on your chart ruler if you have Libra rising, since Venus rules the sign on your Ascendant. So the card's planet is the one that shapes your whole manner, which is usually gracious, friendly and very good at making a room comfortable. This version of Venus has gone into Aquarius, and she's brought a sharper tongue with her. The trine between the two signs means it comes to you easily. You can be charming and cutting in the same sentence, and people often don't notice the cut until they're home.

Libra rising tends to win first encounters by being agreeable. With this card you'll also win them by being clever, holding a position with a smile on your face. It works, and it's a bit dangerous, because the other person feels outmanoeuvred without being able to point to anything you did wrong. There's nothing rude to object to. Air meeting air turns up what's already in your style, and you'll want to watch for the moment when diplomacy becomes a way of getting your own way.

In a negotiation you close the deal so pleasantly that the other side only realises what they gave up a week later. At a new job everyone likes you and trusts you a little less than you'd expect. A first date ends with a gentle disagreement that you won, and they go home feeling slightly handled. With the next person you meet, say one thing you actually think that they might not like, and let it sit there for a moment.
rising.reversed:
The smile starts to look like a strategy on a Libra Ascendant with this card upside down. You're so careful to seem pleasant that new people can't tell what you really think, and some of them stop trusting it. Or you've been caught out lately in someone else's clever game, and you're agreeing with everyone on first meeting so you won't be the target again.

It tends to show at work, in meetings where you nod along and then disagree later in an email. At parties you're everyone's friend and nobody's first call the next day. Around a new partner's friends you work so hard to be liked that you come across as nervous. Let yourself disagree once, early, in a small friendly way, with someone you've just met.

sun.upright:
Scorpio Suns don't lose, or at least they don't let anyone see it, and the Five of Swords is a card about winning and what winning does to people. So it lands on you with some force. You want to be known as someone with depth and nerve, someone who can't be fooled, and there's a part of you that quite likes the look on the face of the man in the card, gathering up everyone else's swords. Your sign is ruled by Mars in the traditional system. You've got the stomach for a fight.

Venus is in detriment in Scorpio, which means the planet of affection works against the grain in your sign. Love in you goes deep and gets possessive, and it doesn't forget a betrayal. Add the square from Aquarius, two fixed signs at right angles, and you have the standoff where neither person will blink. The card's side argues coolly on principle. Your side argues from a wound. Air and water don't naturally understand each other, and the other person's calm can infuriate you, because it looks like they don't care, while your intensity feels to them like an attack.

There's probably a rival at work you've been watching for a year, and the moment has come to be right about them. In a relationship it's the argument where you bring up the thing from three years ago, because you've been saving it. Over money it's refusing to split a debt evenly on principle. Ask yourself who you'd be without this particular enemy, and give that some honest thought before the next round.
sun.reversed:
A grudge is the usual shape of this card reversed on a Scorpio Sun. The fight's long over for everyone else, and you're still holding on to it, quietly, the way you'd keep a card you might need to play later. Venus in detriment has nowhere gentle to put the hurt, so it stays sharp. Sometimes the grudge is against yourself, over a fight you won unfairly and haven't admitted to anyone.

The colleague you've written off gets perfect, icy courtesy. A relative who crossed you years ago still doesn't know you know. Your partner keeps sitting a test you set to see whether they'll let you down again. Pick one old score and settle it for good, either by talking to them or by deciding, in writing, that it's closed.

moon.upright:
Trust is the whole thing for a Scorpio Moon. You need to know exactly where you stand with the people close to you, and you'll test them, sometimes without meaning to, until you're sure. This card in your tides points to a conflict with someone you let in, and it's hit a nerve. Venus is at a disadvantage in Scorpio, in detriment there, so the ordinary comforts of affection don't reach you easily. A hug after a row doesn't fix it. You need the truth first.

Aquarius squares Scorpio. Both are fixed signs, so both dig in, and the card's detached, reasonable manner is exactly what makes your Moon feel unsafe. When someone goes calm and logical on you in a fight, you don't feel reassured. You feel shut out, and a shut door makes a Scorpio Moon want to know what's behind it. Venus does rule part of your sign, the last ten degrees, which belong to the Seven of Cups, cups floating in cloud with a different fantasy in each. That's the trap here. You'll lie awake building versions of what they really meant, most of which never happened.

Between partners it can be jealousy with nothing solid under it, or closeness withdrawn to make a point, and sex is often where the distance shows first. A close friend lets you down in some small way and you say nothing and keep track. Your sleep takes the damage. Ask the person the one question you're afraid to ask, straight out, and believe the answer unless you get real evidence against it.
moon.reversed:
Everything goes inward when a Scorpio Moon draws this card reversed. You were hurt, you've told no one, and the feeling has gone somewhere deep where it's quietly deciding how you'll treat that person from here on. Venus in detriment turns love into watchfulness. You're watching them, and it's tiring for both of you even if they haven't noticed yet.

The body carries it as a tight chest and poor sleep. At home there's a cold spell nobody's allowed to mention. In a friendship it can be cutting someone off in one clean move after years of closeness, without a word of explanation. Before you close a door on anyone, tell one person outside the situation the whole story, and listen to what they make of it.

rising.upright:
Very little gets given away on first meeting with Scorpio rising, and people sense they're being assessed. This card gives the assessment a competitive edge. You're working out who has the power in the room, who's bluffing and what they want, and you're usually right. Venus struggles in your rising sign, where she's in detriment, so easy charm isn't how you open. Your warmth turns up later, for the people who've earned it.

There's a twist in your chart that matters here. With Scorpio rising, Taurus sits on the seventh house, and Venus rules Taurus, so the planet in this card also runs your partnerships and your open rivalries. Aquarius squares Scorpio, and the card's cool, clever style rubs against yours. When someone new tries to outthink you in public, you go very still. That stillness wins a lot of arguments on its own, and it frightens people a bit. You'd be surprised how often Scorpio rising gets called intimidating by people it barely spoke to.

Your first meeting at a new job might be the one where you said four words and the manager decided you were difficult. In a negotiation you hold the silence until the other side gives something away, which works and leaves them wary of you. On a date the intensity of your attention is something some people love and some find too much. Try showing one small, harmless weakness in the first half hour with someone new. Admit you're nervous, or that you got lost on the way there.
rising.reversed:
The guard comes up too early when this card flips on a Scorpio Ascendant. You meet people already braced for a trick, and they feel the suspicion before you've said a word. Or you've been beaten at something in public lately and you're hiding it well, too well, so you come across as cold and unreachable when underneath you're sore.

New workplaces pick up on it, and so do new partners, especially with Venus ruling your seventh house and struggling in your first. You leave a gathering having learned everything about everyone and told them nothing. Online a stranger's comment reads as an attack, and you answer it like one. Next time you catch yourself sizing someone up as a threat, ask them a genuinely curious question and listen to the whole answer.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns like to be the one who says what everyone else is too polite to say, and they're proud of it. The Five of Swords gives you the chance to do exactly that, and to be right, and then to find out that some people didn't want the truth delivered quite like that. You want to be seen as honest, free and a bit larger than life. Venus in your sign is a guest who takes her tone from Jupiter, so your affection is generous and big-hearted and sometimes careless with the details.

Aquarius sits a sextile from Sagittarius and air feeds fire, so the card's cool certainty and your hot conviction get on very well. Too well, sometimes. Put an Aquarian principle together with a Sagittarian's faith in their own opinion and you can hold forth on how things ought to be with total confidence, and leave behind a table of people who've decided it isn't worth arguing with you. A sextile is an opening that still has to be used. Here, the card gives you a real chance to say something true, and it's up to you whether you say it in a way people can take.

At a family dinner it's the political argument you won and the aunt who left early. A manager gets told their strategy was wrong, correctly, in a group email. A friend hears your blunt verdict on their relationship, which they didn't ask for and haven't forgiven. Before you deliver the next hard truth, ask the person whether they want your honest view. If they say no, keep it to yourself.
sun.reversed:
Preaching to an empty room is where this card reversed can leave a Sagittarius Sun. You've been so sure of your view that people have stopped engaging with it, and you've taken their silence for agreement. Or it's gone the opposite way, a public knock to an opinion you cared about, and now you're cynical about everything, and with Venus borrowing Jupiter's size, even the cynicism is loud.

At work there may be a project you've mentally walked away from while you keep turning up. With friends it's the pub argument you keep starting because you lost the last one. Your partner hears you talk about leaving whenever things get hard. Find someone who disagrees with you and ask them to explain their view properly, then say it back to them until they agree you've got it.

moon.upright:
There needs to be room to move for a Sagittarius Moon to feel all right. A trip on the calendar, a door left open, some reason to be hopeful. Conflict makes you restless. You'll laugh it off, change the subject or go for a very long walk, anything to stop a heavy conversation settling on you. So when the Five of Swords turns up in your tides, there's probably a quarrel you've been trying to outrun, and it's kept pace.

Venus is only a visitor in Sagittarius and takes her mood from Jupiter, so your feelings run big and warm and forgive quickly. The card's Venus is the Aquarian kind, cool and principled. The two signs are a sextile apart and air feeds fire, so her logic gets into you easily, and it stirs you up as much as it calms you. That can help. You'll see the argument from a height and understand it. It can also mean you think a hurt through until it seems silly, tell yourself you're above it, and then snap at someone over nothing a week later.

You might have left the last row by booking a weekend away on your own, which helped you and did nothing for your partner. A friend hears you joke about something that clearly still stings. Your body tells you through restlessness, and through not being able to sit through a film. Stay in the room for the whole of the next difficult conversation, even if you have to go for a walk straight after.
moon.reversed:
Suddenly there's a plan, a new course, a trip, a serious look at moving cities. For a Sagittarius Moon that's often what a hurt turns into when this card comes up reversed, and from the inside, running feels a lot like freedom. Or the usual optimism sours, and you go through a patch of being cutting and cynical about the person who upset you, turning it all into jokes nobody else finds funny.

Home can start to feel too small and a relationship like a cage. Friends hear a lot about how you're totally fine. At work there's a sudden impatience with your whole field. Your sleep gets restless, often with vivid dreams. Before you book anything or quit anything, write down what the fight was actually about, in two sentences. Then decide whether the plan still looks as good.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising walks in friendly and a bit loud, and people usually warm to it fast. Draw the Five of Swords here and the friendliness gets a sharp edge. You say what you think, and you think quickly, and with the sextile from Aquarius and air feeding fire, the card's clever, contrarian streak catches in you straight away. New people find you funny and a bit reckless with your opinions.

Jupiter rules your rising sign, which makes him your chart ruler, and Venus in Sagittarius is a visitor who takes her tone from him. Everything you do at first meeting comes out a size larger, the laugh, the story, the strong opinion about the band that's playing. With this card that can tip into winning debates with people you've only just met, and not noticing that they weren't debating. You meant it as fun. Some of them will have gone home thinking you were arrogant, and you'll find out months later, if at all.

In your first week somewhere new, you share an opinion about how things should be run, and you may well be right, and the old hands go wary. At dinner with a partner's friends there's the story that got a big laugh at somebody's expense. Travelling, it's the argument with a local about their own country. The next time you're somewhere new, ask two questions for every opinion you give, and see how much more people tell you.
rising.reversed:
Bluntness runs ahead of a Sagittarius Ascendant when the card comes up reversed. You meet new people with an opinion already in hand, it comes out before the hello, and they file you as combative. Or your confidence has been dented by a public argument and you're unusually guarded, which on a sign known for its openness reads as distant.

Interviews, first dates and new groups bring it out. You're either running the conversation or strangely flat in it. People who've known you for years are used to your directness, and people who've known you ten minutes aren't. Online it's the reply fired at a stranger that you'd never say to their face. Pick one first meeting and go in with no opinions at all, only questions, and notice how differently it goes.

sun.upright:
Playing the long game is what a Capricorn Sun does best, and you'd like to be known as the person who gets there in the end, by hard work and good sense. This is a short-game card. It's the win you snatch today that costs you something you'll want in five years, and a Capricorn Sun usually knows better. That's what makes it interesting when you draw it. Something has tempted you into a fight your better judgement would have walked past.

Aquarius and Capricorn sit side by side on the wheel, and in the traditional scheme Saturn rules them both. So the card's Venus, only a visitor in Aquarius, is coloured by Saturn there, and she'd be coloured by Saturn in your sign too. That's why this card's coldness feels familiar. Affection that shows itself through duty, keeping score, being fair to the letter. Air and earth are opposed, though. The card fights with arguments and principles, you fight with results and patience, and when a Capricorn decides the other side is all talk, you can be quite ruthless about proving it.

At work it could be the promotion you got by outlasting a colleague, and the friendship that didn't survive it. In the family you're the responsible one, and you remind everyone of it in a way that's accurate and a bit cruel. Your partner loses the argument about money because you've got the spreadsheet. Before the next hard-nosed decision, think about who you'll need on your side a few years from now, and whether this helps.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, the card can show a Capricorn Sun grinding on with a conflict out of sheer stubbornness. You've put in too much to back down, so you don't, even though nobody remembers any more what the original disagreement was. Saturn colours Venus in your sign, and in this card she's dutiful and cold and very good at holding a line past the point where it's useful.

The formal complaint you're still pursuing on principle is one version. Being correct and alone at Christmas is another. Then there's the dispute over a small sum that has cost you far more in time than it was ever worth. Put a date in your diary a month out and decide that by then this is either resolved or dropped. Then stick to it the way you stick to everything.

moon.upright:
Emotional safety for a Capricorn Moon comes from being in control of things. Bills paid, the plan in place, nobody leaning on you who shouldn't be. You don't go in for big displays of feeling, and you'd prefer the people around you didn't either. The Five of Swords stirs up a conflict you can't simply manage, and a feeling you can't manage is the thing a Capricorn Moon trusts least.

Venus is a guest in your Moon's sign and takes her colour from Saturn, who also rules Aquarius in the traditional scheme, so you and this card share a certain reserve. You'll understand the Aquarian tactic of going cool and principled in an argument, because you do it too. Where it goes wrong is the opposition of air and earth. The card argues. Your Moon needs proof, and keeps quiet while it waits for some. So you may seem to have accepted an apology and still be holding back trust for months, watching to see if they meant it. It feels like prudence to you, and to the other person it can feel like being on probation for something they've already said sorry for.

Your partner broke a promise, and since then the house has run perfectly and they've had nothing from you. A parent may still be at the root of it, an old pattern where approval only came with achievement. Your body keeps it in the shoulders and jaw. Say, out loud and specifically, what the other person would need to do for you to trust them again. Then give them the chance to do it.
moon.reversed:
Buttoning it all down is how a Capricorn Moon handles this card reversed. The argument hurt, so you work longer hours, tidy up the finances and decide feelings are a luxury. Saturn's reserve colours Venus in your sign, and in this reversed card it turns into coldness, the kind the people close to you feel as a draught under the door.

At home everything runs well and nobody's having any fun. Intimacy gets put off for work, week after week. Friends ask how you are and get a very competent answer that tells them nothing. Your sleep gets shallow and early. Tell the person you were hurt, in one sentence, without explaining why you had every right to be. Then let them respond without managing it.

rising.upright:
People often assume Capricorn rising is older than it is, or further up the ladder, because you meet the world looking composed, competent and a bit reserved. Put this card on top of that and the composure gets harder. You come across as someone who doesn't lose, and who wouldn't be much bothered about making someone else lose. Most of the time that's unfair on you, but it's how it reads.

Saturn rules your rising sign, and Saturn is the traditional ruler of Aquarius as well, so the card's cool Aquarian Venus and your own manner have something in common. Both stand back, size things up, and keep feelings out of the negotiation. Otherwise Capricorn and Aquarius are neighbours with little in common, each with what the other lacks, and air and earth pull against each other. The card brings the clever argument. You bring the patience to outlast whoever's making it. In a first encounter you'll often win simply by not reacting, which works well and is quite chilly to be on the other end of.

Starting somewhere new, you can pick up a reputation as tough within the first month, fair or not. In a negotiation you hold firm on every point, get the lot, and the other side won't work with you again. A first date wonders whether you're even enjoying yourself, you're so self-contained. With someone new, let them see you laugh at something early. The rest of the meeting tends to go differently after that.
rising.reversed:
The composure can harden into armour when this card reverses on a Capricorn Ascendant. You go into new situations expecting to be undercut, and you make sure nobody can, which leaves people nothing to connect to. Or you've been outplayed somewhere visible and gone extra formal, very correct, all business. People read the correctness as coldness and the coldness as disapproval.

It shows at work first, especially with anyone above you. At a party you talk only about your job. A new partner waits a long time for the professional manner to drop, and wonders whether it ever will. At your next first meeting, share one small thing that isn't going well for you, lightly, and let it be part of the conversation.

sun.upright:
This card belongs to your sign. It's the card of the first ten degrees of Aquarius, the decan Venus rules, so for an Aquarius Sun it's a piece of your own sign speaking, and if your Sun sits in those first ten degrees, it's the card of your actual Sun. You want to be known for your mind, your independence, your willingness to stand by an unpopular view. This card is what that looks like when the view has started to matter to you more than the person across from you.

Venus has no special dignity in Aquarius. She's a visitor, coloured by Saturn in the old system and by Uranus in the modern one, which makes your affection loyal, principled and quite cool. You love humanity and you're a bit awkward with a crying friend. You and the card share an element, so it turns up the volume on what's already there. The detachment that makes you fair in a crisis can make you cold in an argument, and you often don't notice the moment it switches. You're sure you're being reasonable. The other person feels they've been given a lecture.

In a meeting you stood on a principle while a colleague's job was on the line. In a group chat you were right about some cause and quietly lost two people. Your partner only wanted you on their side, and you won the debate instead. Next time you're sure you're right, look at who's in the room first, and at what they're hoping to hear from you.
sun.reversed:
Standing alone on principle can harden into just standing alone, and that's where this card reversed tends to find an Aquarius Sun. You've won enough arguments, or refused to concede enough of them, that people have stopped arguing with you and gone somewhere they're welcome. You may be telling yourself that's fine, since you never needed the crowd.

At work you're the lone dissenter again, and nobody's asking your opinion first any more. There's a group of friends you've drifted from because they got too conventional for you. In the family there's an argument you refuse to reopen, on principle. Get in touch with one person you fell out with over an idea and talk about anything else, with no mention of who was right.

moon.upright:
Distance is how an Aquarius Moon handles feelings. You need space, friends who don't crowd you, and the freedom to think a thing through before anyone asks how you feel about it. This card is part of your own sign, its first ten degrees, so in your tides it speaks your language exactly. That makes it familiar. It also means it amplifies a habit you already have.

When there's a conflict, you go cool. It's how you stay safe. You work out the principle, decide who was fair and who wasn't, file it away, and the feeling underneath gets left in a drawer. Venus in Aquarius takes her colour from Saturn, and Saturn likes things kept at a distance and in order. The people close to you can find it hard to reach you after a fight, even when you've honestly moved on, because what they needed was to see that it mattered to you.

Your partner gets a calm, fair discussion after a row and comes away feeling you didn't care. When one friend upsets you, you withdraw from the whole group. A parent asks if you're all right and gets a very sensible answer about something else. Your sleep turns light and your mind won't stop. Say how you felt, using an actual feeling word, before you say what you think.
moon.reversed:
The cool goes cold when an Aquarius Moon meets this card reversed. You've detached so well from a hurt that you've detached from the person too, and they can feel it. Or it tips the other way and you get unexpectedly stirred up about a principle, a cause or somebody else's unfair treatment, which is easier to be angry about than your own thing.

At home there's a housemate or partner you've gone polite with. Friends notice you've gone missing from the group chat without explanation. Online it's the argument with strangers that eats an evening. Your sleep and your appetite go irregular. Tell one close person, in plain words, that the fight got to you. Aquarius Moons tend to find that saying it once does most of the work.

rising.upright:
First impressions of Aquarius rising tend to be of someone friendly, a bit unusual and hard to read, and this card is your own sign's, turning up at the door. It's the first decan of Aquarius. The cool, clever debater in it is a version of how you meet people, only louder. You come across as quick, independent and slightly above the fray, and some people take that as a challenge.

Air on air amplifies. You'll hold your own in any first exchange, and you enjoy an argument with a stranger more than you probably should, because it's how you find out how someone thinks. Venus is a visitor in your rising sign, coloured by Saturn, so your charm is real but kept at arm's length. With Aquarius rising, Leo sits on the seventh house, so the people you end up opposite are often warm, proud and quick to feel slighted. A cool, clever win in the first conversation is exactly what a Leo sort of person takes personally.

A new colleague gets debated on their first day and decides you think you're smarter than everyone. At a party you're the contrarian voice in a friendly conversation, which you found stimulating and they found tiring. You win a disagreement about a film and lose the second date. Let the next person you meet win the first small argument, even one you're sure about, and see what it opens up.
rising.reversed:
Aloofness is the risk for an Aquarius Ascendant with the card reversed. You hang back in new company, watching, and people read it as superiority. Or a recent clash has made you prickly, and you come into new rooms ready to disagree with whatever's said first, just to show you're nobody's follower.

Work picks it up in a new team or with a new client. At an event you spend the whole time talking ideas with one person, and the host feels you snubbed everyone else. With Leo on your seventh house, new partners may feel you're not that interested in them. In your next few first meetings, show some warmth early, a real compliment or a bit of genuine enthusiasm, even if it feels slightly out of character.

sun.upright:
Venus is exalted in Pisces. She's an honoured guest there, love at its most generous and ready to forgive, and a Pisces Sun tends to want to be known for exactly that, kindness, imagination, seeing the best in people. The card is Venus from the sign just before yours, Aquarius, where she has no special standing and cares a great deal about principle and about keeping track of who was fair.

Pisces and Aquarius are neighbours on the wheel with little in common beyond the fence. Each has what the other lacks, and air and water don't naturally mix. For you, drawing this card often means you're in a conflict you didn't choose and don't know how to fight. Someone has been clever and cool with you, and your instinct is to give way, understand their side and make yourself smaller until it passes. Sometimes it's the other way round, and you were the sharp one, and the guilt is out of all proportion. I've met very few Pisces Suns who enjoy winning an argument, even one they needed to win.

A colleague took credit for your idea, and you decided not to make a fuss. You apologised to your partner for something that wasn't your fault because the tension was unbearable. In the family, everyone else's arguments seem to get poured into you. Next time you feel yourself giving way, ask what you'd tell a friend in the same spot. Then do that.
sun.reversed:
You lost the argument by handing it over, and a Pisces Sun with this card reversed can end up quietly suffering about it, which is its own way of keeping the fight alive. Venus exalted in your sign can overdo the forgiveness until there's nothing left of your own view. Or the hurt goes into escape, more sleep, more screen, another glass, anything that blurs it.

After a conflict at work you take on the extra load so nobody's upset with you. You say yes to plans you don't want because you once said no and it went badly. You call the long silence with your partner keeping the peace. Say one thing you want, clearly, to one person, and don't apologise for it.

moon.upright:
Moods pass through a Pisces Moon like weather through an open window, yours and everyone else's. You need gentleness, time alone, music, water, people who don't shout. The Five of Swords brings a conflict into your tides, and even if it's someone else's, you'll feel it. Two friends falling out, tension at work, a partner in a cold mood, it all gets into you.

With Venus exalted in your Moon's sign, love in you runs deep and forgiving, almost without limit. The card's Venus is the Aquarian one, next door on the wheel but a stranger in temperament, cool and principled and willing to hurt someone in the name of what's right. Air and water don't clash, and they don't naturally get on either. When this card meets your Moon they get on badly. Logic used against your feelings makes you think the feelings were wrong to have. You go quiet, you give in, or you drift off somewhere in your head where nobody can reach you, and the other person may think the matter's closed.

After the argument where you gave in, you cried in the car. When friends fall out you absorb everyone's version until you don't know what you think. Tiredness is how your body shows it, and needing a lot of extra sleep. Go somewhere near water, or run a long bath, and let yourself feel the whole thing without deciding who was right.
moon.reversed:
Everything goes soft and blurred when the card turns over on a Pisces Moon. The hurt from an argument gets absorbed so thoroughly that you can't find its edges, and you drift. Venus exalted in your sign turns into forgiving someone who hasn't asked to be forgiven, then feeling vaguely sad without knowing why. Pisces Moons are very good at talking themselves out of a fair complaint.

Sleep gets heavy, and escape gets tempting, films, snacks, a drink, long hours on the phone. At home there's tension you've decided not to notice. A friend said something that hurt and you've told yourself you were oversensitive. Write down what happened, only the facts, as if you were explaining it to a stranger. Then read it back the next morning.

rising.upright:
Strangers tell Pisces rising things, usually within ten minutes, because you meet people softly, with a kind face and an open, unguarded manner. The Five of Swords sits awkwardly on that. It's a card of cool, clever conflict, and it usually means you're walking into situations where someone is sharper and warier than you, or where you've had to be.

Venus is exalted in Pisces, so charm at first meeting comes easily and it's genuinely warm. There's a catch in your chart, though. With Pisces rising, Virgo is on your seventh house, and Venus is in fall in Virgo, so the people you end up opposite, partners and rivals both, are often the critical, exacting kind who don't take charm at face value. Add the Aquarian air of this card, which doesn't mix naturally with your water, and you can find yourself being picked apart by someone you tried to be nice to. You may try meeting them with their own coolness and find it doesn't suit you at all.

At work a colleague fact-checks your friendly suggestion in front of everyone. In a new relationship there's their sharp tongue, which you found exciting at first. Online a stranger takes your openness for naivety. Before the next meeting where you expect someone to be sharp with you, decide on one point you won't give ground on, and hold it gently.
rising.reversed:
The soft manner can go vague when this card turns over on a Pisces Ascendant. You're so keen to avoid a clash with new people that you agree with everything, and they come away with no idea who you are. Or someone's cleverness has hurt you and you're coming into new places half-hidden, apologising a lot, taking up as little space as you can.

You'll see it most in new jobs and new groups. You get handed the tasks nobody wants, because you won't say no. On a date you're so accommodating the other person can't tell whether you're interested. With Virgo on your seventh house, you may keep attracting critics. Practise one sentence that says no politely, and use it at least once with somebody new.

1.upright:
How you come across before anyone knows you is first house business. Your face, your walk, the way you start things. It's one of the four angular houses, the corners of the chart, so whatever lands here is visible. With the Five of Swords in the first, the conflict is out in the open and it's written on you. People can see you're braced for a fight, or fresh from one.

Aries is this house's natural sign and Mars its natural ruler, and Aries is a sign where Venus sits in detriment. So the card's planet works against the grain here, and that's real friction. The first house wants to go first, act fast and back yourself. Venus in this card wants to be right about it, coolly and on principle. What comes out can be a sort of quiet aggression, someone pleasant who won't be moved. Aquarius and Aries are sextile, air feeding fire, so your arguments catch quickly and your manner catches with them. You may notice your jaw set, your shoulders up, your answers getting shorter.
